description: The bar chart, titled “Factual Errors,” illustrates the number of questions (out of 40) in which the Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning generated by GPT-3 contained at least one factual error, across four different question-answering datasets — HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC — and three retrieval methods: NoR QA (no retrieval, orange), OneR QA (single retrieval, red), and IRCOT QA (interleaved retrieval with CoT, blue). The vertical y-axis represents the count of questions with factual errors, ranging from 0 to 40 in increments of 5. Each dataset has three adjacent bars corresponding to the retrieval methods, with values labeled atop each bar. For HotpotQA, NoR QA has 15 errors, OneR QA has 10, and IRCOT QA has 5. For 2WikiMQA, the counts are 29 (NoR), 23 (OneR), and 14 (IRCOT). For MuSiQue, they are 28 (NoR), 27 (OneR), and 23 (IRCOT). For IIRC, the values are 15 (NoR), 14 (OneR), and 11 (IRCOT). Visually, the blue bars (IRCOT QA) are consistently the shortest across all datasets, indicating the fewest factual errors, followed by red (OneR QA), then orange (NoR QA), supporting the caption’s claim that factual errors decrease in the order: NoR > OneR > IRCOT. The bars are grouped by dataset along the horizontal axis, with no sorting applied across datasets.
